Now that the United Kingdom has voted to leave the EU, stock markets worldwide have dropped and European stocks have lowered. The Prime Minister is resigning and will allow his successor to begin the leave process, which wouldn't be until October.

We have many weeks/months of uncertainty ahead.

If you play the stocks game with regular investments or cash, this might not be a bad time to buy the temporarily low-priced stock, especially if it's directly investing in English or European companies that have taken a tumble.

In regards to a 401K (or other retirement plan), you probably should just stay put and leave things as you have them (usually in some Target year plan that uses stocks for some of the investments). I definitely don't recommend moving anything to a stable value fund and lose money by selling your stocks, when a recovery could happen in a few months/years.

The Pound is down 10% right now. If you need to acquire a large sum of Pounds for later use, now is a good time to exchange USD for them, just be sure the exchange merchant you use isn't fleecing you.

With the Pound being low, this is also a good time to book that trip to London or Europe, as airfare and hotel costs in the UK have effective dropped due to the lowered Pound. If you've already booked sometime before the Brexit, it doesn't hurt to speak with the airline/hotel/agency and see if you can re-book for cheaper.

Everything that was true yesterday in terms of financial health and rules is the same today. What changed is a view of what the future may hold, but a future that will be negotiated over time and so which can have changes priced in logically as they become certain and known. I personally think Brexit will be good for the British economy and, if they learn the lesson, for the EU economy. Even if I'm wrong, this is not economic Armageddon.

I wish YouTube didn't have such a monopoly on video sharing considering their Take Down, Stay Down bullshit with ContentID, but there are alternatives if you search them out.
